purpose: References for the monthly statistical forecasting capability. Bibliographic data below were verified against the local PDFs where a PDF exists; anything not verifiable locally is marked null/unverified. Paper-derived methodological statements are kept separate from computed results (see evidence/forecast_eval).

references.title: Time Series Prediction of Temperature Using Seasonal ARIMA and LSTM Models
references.venue: Gazi Journal of Engineering Sciences, vol. 9, no. 3, pp. 574-584
references.local_file: research/Time Series Prediction of Temperature Using Seasonal ARIMA and LSTM Models[#1299006]-3150939.pdf
references.read_status: full text read (abstract, method, results, conclusion)
references.bibliographic_note: The running header of the PDF cites the title as 'Time Series Prediction of Temperature Using ARIMA and LSTM Models'; the title page uses 'Seasonal ARIMA and LSTM Models'.
paper_derived_methods: monthly mean temperature, one weather station (Ankara, Turkiye), Jan 2010 - Mar 2023
SARIMA selected with auto_arima: SARIMA(1,0,0)x(2,0,1)12, 12-month seasonality

paper_reported_results.scope: one station, one test block; not a result for any other location

limitations_for_this_project: one station and one split: no rolling origins, no uncertainty on the metrics
no comparison with a seasonal-naive or climatology baseline, so it does not show skill beyond the seasonal cycle
does not evaluate lead-by-lead skill or prediction-interval calibration
does not establish 24-month skill for any location

references.title: Forecasting daily meteorological time series using ARIMA and regression models
paper_derived_methods: daily air temperature and precipitation 1980-2010 at four European sites in different climatic zones (Jokioinen, Dikopshof, Lleida, Lublin)
Box-Jenkins and Holt-Winters seasonal ARIMA, ARIMA with Fourier-term regressors (ARIMAF), time-series regression with trend and seasonality
out-of-sample comparison on a six-year independent test set
authors recommend more than one error measure and note that the best model changes with the data/site
limitations_for_this_project: the best precipitation model depends on the site (so one model for every location is not justified)
a six-year test block is a single evaluation, not rolling-origin

references.title: Predicting Meteorological Variables on Local Level with SARIMA, LSTM and Hybrid Techniques
paper_derived_methods: 3-hourly data from one hotel meteorological station in northern Crete
SARIMA, LSTM and a hybrid; MAE in physical units (degC, %, m/s)
authors report the hybrid improvement was modest relative to its cost (about 2 h of computing)
limitations_for_this_project: horizon of 1-2 days at 3-hourly resolution: it does NOT support or test 24-month monthly forecasts

references.title: A Hybrid SARIMA-LSTM Model for Air Temperature Forecasting
references.read_status: NOT read: no local full text and no legitimate access was available in this work. Only the DOI/URL supplied by the user are recorded; authors, year and venue are unverified and left null. No claim from this paper is used.
limitations_for_this_project: no hybrid or neural candidate is implemented: the data volume (about 540 monthly values per series) and the validation budget do not justify it, and nothing from paper D is relied on

references.title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.), chapters on ARIMA and on the forecasting toolbox
references.read_status: URL only; the pages were not retrieved in this work. The methods used here that are standard textbook practice (benchmark methods, seasonal-naive variance by horizon, MASE, time-series cross-validation, prediction intervals) are implemented from the standard definitions; they are cited as 'standard method', not as page-verified quotations.

references.title: statsmodels SARIMAX / ARIMA / ETSModel documentation
references.read_status: local copies of the SARIMAX and ARIMA pages exist; the installed library is statsmodels 0.15.0
paper_derived_methods: SARIMAX state-space SARIMA with trend and exogenous regressors; forecast intervals from get_forecast().conf_int()
exogenous regressors need values over the forecast horizon
limitations_for_this_project: no exogenous regressors are used in this project: future values are not available at forecast time and no scenarios are defined

not_a_citation_for_numbers: Papers support methodology only. Forecast numbers come from the data (NASA POWER) and the model run recorded in each result; no paper is evidence that a particular future temperature will occur.
